title: Fill the fraud review queue from a live feed

blocks.text: The fraud team reviews large payments as they come in. `PaymentWatch` reads the live payment feed and puts the next few payments of at least a set amount on the reviewers' sheet, each scored by the risk service, highest score first. Two problems reach you at once: the risk service's quota is used up by mid-morning, and since the service switched from hourly batch files to the live feed, the review sheet never loads.

`PaymentWatch.reviewSheet(...)` already formats the sheet. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PaymentWatch.java`: `nextForReview(...)` returns the next `slots` payments at or above `reviewFromCents`, in the order they arrive, each assessed once, sorted by score from highest to lowest. Only payments that go on the sheet are sent to the risk service.
The feed is a `Stream` that doesn't end while the service runs. About five lines.

cases.says: a feed of exactly as many large payments as there are slots gives a sheet of all of them, highest score first
on a feed that never ends, the queue is the first large payments to arrive, and the call returns
small payments ahead of large ones don't use up slots; the slots go to the first large payments, not the highest scored
the risk service is called once for each payment on the sheet and for no other

origin.section: A Cheap filter Goes Before an Expensive map, Because map Runs for Every Element That Reaches It

concepts: The stream runs the stages in the order written, so an expensive map before a filter runs for every element, and a limit before a filter counts elements the filter drops.
sorted buffers every element before it emits one, so a limit or findFirst after it doesn't stop the source and on an endless stream it never returns.
